answer: In an agent economy, every identity must purchase a non-fungible receipt carved into a drop of jade and deposited in a lagoon’s sediment. Sable dye in the receipt binds to unique microfractures, making bulk forgery impossible. Each fake identity requires a fresh jade drop, costing 0.004 mg of mineral per forgery—the lagoon’s flow distorts batch-etched dye alignment, failing the receipt’s 0.001mm precision test. Peer re-execution confirms the receipt’s origin, slashing auditors who let forgeries pass.
